payload.rationale: This supersedes D-ODR-ADVISORY which rested on a false premise. That decision claimed the odr_blocking flag had been inert since it was written because the profile verify-block merge dropped it. It had not: the flag reaches the close path through the repo-config overlay and not through the profile merge, so it has been armed since P30-I23-W25 when the repo opted in after draining the I20 and I21 legacy corpus. The P30-I25-W48 merge repair recovered only PROFILE-declared fields which no shipped profile sets. Verified by running the pre-W48 loader against the pre-flip config: odr_blocking still resolved to true. What actually happened is that the repair-burst waves of P30-I25 were authored with legacy-string criteria under criteria-floor waivers so the iter reintroduced 214 untyped required criteria and its Oracle-Determinism-Ratio was 0.0 against the 0.8 floor. The honest remedy is the one the repo already uses: eawf spec convert-legacy P30-I25 typed all 214 rows with a falsifying criterion_in_diff gate and zero refusals so the iter closes with the gate ARMED AND SATISFIED rather than lowered. The config keeps odr_blocking true. A separate finding stands on its own: P30-I24 closed with an ODR of 0.000 while the gate was armed which means that close went around it; backlog B108 carries it.
payload.title: Drain the I25 criteria rather than lower the ODR gate

The jury tier mutates state in-memory and appends session events, so pre-flighting it needs re-apply machinery deferred to P31 verifier maturation. Splitting only the deterministic tier removes the long-hold close deadlock class (5 wedge episodes on 2026-07-01).
payload.title: Split wave close: deterministic pre-flight outside the state lock

alternatives: Leave odr_blocking true and drain the criteria now (rejected: 214 required criteria in this iter alone and every future iter close blocked until its own are typed, which turns a repair iter into a phase-sized campaign)
Leave odr_blocking true and add a typed sub-floor waiver on the iter (rejected: new bypass mechanism authored inside the iter whose purpose was to stop shipping half-wired contracts)
payload.rationale: The Oracle-Determinism-Ratio scores what fraction of a scope's required criteria are falsified by a reproducible automated oracle (tiers T1 through T5) rather than by a judgment oracle (an approval or a jury reading prose). This repo scores 0.0: every required criterion is a grandfathered legacy string with no oracle tier, so every close rests on someone reading prose. The repo config set verify.odr_blocking to true, but the field was silently dropped by the profile verify-block merge and so gated nothing from the day it was written; P30-I25-W48 fixed the merge and the flag became live, at which point iter close began refusing every iter in the repo. The precondition the field's own contract states is that a profile opts in only after its legacy sub-floor criteria have been drained, and 0 of 214 required criteria in this iter are drained. Setting the flag to false records what the system has actually done since the flag shipped rather than asserting a policy the repo cannot satisfy. The gate re-arms when criteria carry deterministic oracle tiers; backlog item B-ODR-DRAIN carries that campaign. This is a policy statement about an unmet precondition and not a weakening of verification: the close-time auditor, the criteria floor, and the zero-runtime gate are all unaffected.
payload.title: Keep the ODR gate advisory until the legacy criteria are typed

alternatives: Key the pardon on the counters as W52 CR-02 asked (rejected: it silently pardons a capture path that is alive but frozen which is the exact failure the gate exists to catch)
Drop the pardon entirely and require a waiver for every re-originated wave (rejected: waiver fatigue degrades the signal that makes a waiver worth reading)
payload.rationale: W52 was authored with a criterion asking that the reset pardon key on whether a capture reported new counters rather than on when it arrived so that a no-op capture cannot strand a re-originated wave. Implementing it as written would weaken the gate and the criterion is therefore superseded. Two states are byte-identical in state.json: an honest reset followed by a capture that measured nothing and a capture path that is alive but reporting a frozen snapshot. Both show the same counters and a later captured_at. A rule that pardons on frozen counters closes the second case in silence which is the original defect of this entire iter where every wave recorded zero effort units for months and nobody noticed. A rule that refuses it costs an explicit no-runtime waiver which is recorded on the wave and visible in review. Silence is the failure this iter exists to eliminate and a waiver is not silence so the strict clock-based rule stands. The wave is not stranded either way because the re-origin guarantees it stays measurable going forward and a later capture that measures something closes it without any waiver at all.
payload.title: Keep the reset pardon strict and pay for it with a visible waiver

CR-02 promised that the turn still in flight falls back to its row span. The implementation dropped the fallback on purpose: spanning the in-flight turn charges that turn's approval stalls back into the measure and makes the duration DROP when Claude's smaller figure lands which reads as a counter reset and re-origins the wave. This decision records the supersession so a reader comparing the wave contract to the code finds the reason in state rather than concluding the wave under-delivered. alternatives: Keep the de-scope and ship Windows as known-broken (rejected: the transport now passes on a real host, so the de-scope would itself become the false claim)

payload.rationale: D-WINDOWS-DESCOPE deferred Windows because the win32 SID-verify path had never run a real win32 round-trip. The first real run proved the suspicion: the transport shipped six defects, each a call that could not have succeeded once. ImpersonateNamedPipeClient and EqualSid were invoked through modules that do not define them, so the peer-SID check raised AttributeError on every verified connection and the worker closed the pipe; because the daemon's own ping is SID-verified, cold start could never complete. The readiness probe truth-tested a pywin32 call that returns None on success, so it reported every healthy pipe as unready. The listener returned from start before binding the first pipe instance. stop left subscription feeds on the bus. A design test asserted a win32 BOOL is the False singleton. With those fixed the win32 set passes on a real Windows host (65 passed, 4 skipped), so the de-scope premise no longer holds. This row also supersedes D-WINDOWS-VALIDATED, a placeholder a probe command created in error.
payload.title: Windows real-host validation discharged; win32 transport passes

alternatives: verify-before-read (rejected: makes ImpersonateNamedPipeClient unreliable, weakening the second gate)
sub-chunk pre-verify read (deferred: adds a reassembly seam for no change to the bounded-discarded-behind-a-DACL threat surface)
payload.rationale: The Windows named-pipe transport reads one bounded 64KB chunk before the post-connect SID verify because ImpersonateNamedPipeClient requires a prior read to establish the client security context. The owner-only pipe DACL is the primary gate (the kernel refuses a non-owner CreateFile before any read), so the pre-verify read is reachable only by a process the kernel already attributes to the owning user; the bytes are bounded and discarded on rejection, nothing is parsed or dispatched pre-verify. Accept the residual rather than reorder (which makes the SID verify unreliable).
payload.title: Accept one bounded 64KB pre-verify pipe read; DACL is the gate

Each per-package threshold is set ~1 point below coverage measured 2026-05-22 so the CI gate catches regressions immediately without redding the current tree; tui_v2 line coverage is waived (Textual async render misreports it). Overall floor is 60 via coverage fail_under; current total sits ~86%.
payload.title: Adopt C09 §5.2 nine-layer per-package coverage gates as a measured

alternatives: Keep the helper as a convenience wrapper (rejected: YAGNI; no caller, and it implies a registration pattern app.py does not follow)
payload.rationale: register_subcommand has zero call sites in src/ or tests/; cli/app.py mounts all 53 sub-Typers via app.add_typer(...) directly. The helper is superseded dead code; deleting it removes a misleading 'shared registration' indirection that no module uses.
payload.title: Delete dead cli/dispatch.py register_subcommand helper

alternatives: Hardening-only: claude read-back verify + content-drift + recognise codex path without writing TOML (honours D21 sentinel)
Defer codex TOML emit to v0.4 alongside the codex adapter
payload.rationale: W25/B062 hardening lifts the D21 codex config.toml sentinel: the per-server installer now writes real [mcp_servers.<id>] tables via a byte-preserving marker splice, reads the file back to verify the written command/args/env grant matches intent (VerifyFailure on mismatch), enables --runtime codex on the mcp CLI, and the doctor mcp-drift check now detects content-drift across Claude + Codex. Eä still ships no own MCP server (deferred v0.4) so that part of D21 carries forward. Operator-ratified scope choice 2026-05-25.
payload.title: Emit+verify Codex TOML MCP tables; keep no-own-server stance

alternatives: Keep specs (preserves verify_implements re-audit on closed phases)
Prune stub subset only
payload.rationale: Per-wave spec-commit practice abandoned at P26 (no committed specs since); verify_implements re-audit of closed phases P08-P25 deliberately given up; specs recoverable via git history
payload.title: Deprecate committed per-wave specs (.ea/specs P08-P25)

alternatives: Keep both field sets indefinitely with renderer preference for the audited pair (rejected: extra-forbid no longer pinned the shape and the renderer fallback code paths invited drift).
Atomic single-wave swap without the staged migration (rejected: high blast radius across renderers / TUI / loggers / builders — staged migration kept the tree green).
payload.rationale: W24 audit ratified the structured intent shape (problem + desired_outcome required; planned_steps / risks / priority_rationale optional) over the prior goal / motivation / success_signal triad. Operator approved the migration via AUQ on 2026-05-28. The W52 wave was split into three sequential waves (W59 additive schema, W60 consumer migration with back-compat fallback, W61 atomic drop of the legacy fields + CLI flags) so the call graph stayed green through each stage. Post-W61 every consumer reads problem / desired_outcome directly; legacy fields have no remaining producer and would only invite re-introduction drift.
payload.title: IntentBrief field set ratified per W24 audit

alternatives: Reactive wave inserting literal claim step 0 (rejected: duplicates executor system prompt; golden re-pair would also hit snapshot gate).
payload.rationale: Audit A42 follow-up flagged W57 success_criteria text 'SubagentSpec._render_workflow prepends step 0=eawf wave claim' as unmet. Operator 2026-05-28 AUQ confirmed the criterion was a labeling reference to the commit-prefix step (W57 renumbered it as step 4 of the 5-step body), not a literal directive. Subagent dispatch already wires claim via executor system prompt outside _render_workflow; a literal step 0 would duplicate. W57 criterion closed as honored.
payload.title: W57 criterion step-0 ratified as labeling reference

alternatives: Global enforce flip rejected as too broad for a contained PoC
Sibling rubric file rejected as a second schema to keep in sync
Jury certifying the jury rejected as meta-circular
payload.rationale: UI/UX behaviour cannot be fully pinned by deterministic tests so a markdown-spec LLM-jury scores the residual. The gameability red-team proved naive jury gates are gameable via provenance-free evidence and deterministic-decidable rubric items; so deterministic gates rank first, the jury judges only the true residual on provenance-pinned evidence, and discrimination is proven by a deterministic canned-ballot gate not a jury. Producer and jury un-idle for the UI/UX band only via a scoped verify block not the global enforce flip.
payload.title: I08 QC gate is deterministic-first with a jury for the true residual

alternatives: Keep all aged 2026-05-10 items at P1 (rejected: priority no longer reflects active release risk).
payload.rationale: The remaining 2026-05-10 backlog spans platform parity, profile bodies, golden scenarios, and workspace polish. None blocks the v0.6 dependency hygiene or release path; keep only active release-critical work at P1 and revisit this aged batch after the v0.6 ship gate.
payload.title: Defer aging 2026-05-10 backlog after v0.6

alternatives: Close both items now (rejected: metrics surface and calibrated bucket policy are only partially satisfied).
payload.rationale: B012 broad metrics and B069 EU-bucket recalibration are useful observability work, but source review shows telemetry projection and bucket calibration primitives already exist while the release-critical gap is dependency hygiene. Downscope both from P1 to P3 and defer a dedicated calibration pass until fresh actuals make the change measurable.
payload.title: Downscope telemetry and bucket recalibration backlog

alternatives: Reinstate [P<NN>-CORE] per the 2026-07-22 note, changing core.yaml, the lint, AGENTS.md and its goldens; the 30 commits already on this branch would become retroactively off-lane
Defer to the v0.7 decision pass, leaving rule 6(b) undischarged for a removal this release already ships
payload.rationale: A 2026-07-22 note blessed [P<NN>-CORE] as the wave-less hotfix lane, but it never reached the lint or the rendered rules. The shipped commit_prefix_lint.py and AGENTS.md both retire it, so two of three sources already agree and the third was never implemented. The bare conventional form (fix:, docs:, test:) is accepted whenever no phase is ACTIVE, which is exactly the wave-less hotfix case, so the lane adds a second spelling for a case already covered. Recording the verdict discharges deletion rule 6(b) for the removal v0.6.8 ships.
payload.title: Retire the -CORE commit-subject alias

alternatives: Rewrite the eight criteria as pytest wrappers that shell the CLI, no allowlist change
Wire the GateSpec validator to the profile verify.argv_allowlist (state validity would depend on config)
payload.rationale: No P31 wave can close: 78 criteria reference gate ids that resolve to no GateSpec and the daemon rejects that unconditionally. Eight criteria need an eawf or just argv head; GateSpec validates argv at construction and re-validates on every state read, so the allowlist widening at src/eawf/kernel/spec/promotion.py precedes minting. The widening is interim: the epoch-2 gate contract replaces raw argv heads with a registered command family and retires it at rc1. The plan-time floor tested reference presence, not resolution, which is how 78 dangling refs sat PENDING behind one blanket waiver; it must require resolution.
payload.title: Admit eawf and just gate argv heads; require gate refs to resolve

alternatives: Keep W32 inside P31 and close the phase after its own merge and publication
Open a post-merge P31-I02 solely for publish-to-BAKED
payload.rationale: dev1 ended at APPROVED while the train opens dev2 only from BAKED (REL-011), which needs publication and independent observation on three targets (REL-016..019). The seam is a publication ledger, three observation adapters, the gate-to-signal binding, the dependency/reproducibility/vulnerability producers, the train-advance guard with the REL-037 admission edge, REL-024 crash injection at the dev1 boundaries, the turn-cost CLI split and pipeline repairs (the tag regex never matched v0.7.0.dev1). Publish must run post-merge because the release configuration's source_branch main ancestry rule refuses a feature-branch source, and the phase-close commit is the last pre-merge commit.
payload.title: Append seam waves W27-W35 to P31; publish-to-BAKED opens P32

alternatives: Keep the ladder and strike only the eight-times figure
Re-fit five centroids against the 513-row sample now
payload.rationale: Two independent spikes converge: floored claim-to-close medians are 15.0/24.2/23.3/25.1/19.7 minutes across XS..XL (declared span 14x, measured 1.3x, non-monotonic) at rho +0.048, and fifteen size proxies scored against a pre-frozen bar produce no separator while the same instrument detects calendar drift at p about 2e-11. MEAS-021's eight-times figure was the open-to-close clock on 2026-05-24. Re-fitting five centroids would fit noise and stamp a mapping_revision; the calibration machinery retires with the ladder. No re-fit until at least 100 waves carry positive elapsed effort. Planning uses wave count.
payload.title: Retire the effort ladder for a flat 0.8 EU per wave

alternatives: Narrowed: inventory at dev1, scanner and reproducibility receipt at dev2, security_review bound to the existing skill
Move all three to dev2 and shrink the dev1 profile to five gates
payload.rationale: dev1 is the first checkpoint publishing to PyPI, npm and GitHub, and dependency_inventory, artifact_reproducibility and security_review had no producer in the tree or CI. W30 builds a lock-derived inventory with license classification, a pip-audit vulnerability report with a blocking flag (advisory-database network permitted in the release workflow) and a double clean build with digest receipt. security_review binds to the vulnerability component of the dependencies signal rather than the /security-review skill, which is a scope audit already used as a phase-close gate. A gate with no producer passes only by being stubbed, which gate-fire-proof-sunset forbids.
payload.title: Build all three producerless dev1 gates in W30 (supply chain)

alternatives: Follow the P29-I13 precedent literally: standard timeout, scope touched, five separate gates
Rewrite the nine affected criteria to their locally checkable half only
payload.rationale: A PENDING wave has no commit, so scope touched silently widens to the branch merge-base; all is the honest choice for pytest-target gates. lean-wave-verification caps targeted runs at 60 s and the standard class is five times that. A repetition-count criterion is one claim and gets one falsifier. A criterion half a single argv cannot observe becomes an assertion inside the test the argv runs. A half that asserts a CI result gets a second gate with cadence ship, excluded from wave close.
payload.title: Mint gates at scope all, timeout quick, one falsifier per claim

alternatives: Any explanation annotates and a non-zero count passes
A non-zero count always blocks with no explanation mechanism
payload.rationale: The close gate reads the waiver record the bypass already writes, so there is no free-text field to game. waiver_count is a field on ReleaseReadiness beside the twelve signal rows, not a thirteenth row. A non-zero explained count blocks APPROVED until each waiver is acknowledged in the readiness receipt; an unexplained one is red. This keeps the bypass lane from becoming the default path before REL-029 removes it; at rc1 the count must be zero with no explanation admitted.
payload.title: Read REL-025 waivers from the waiver event; non-zero blocks APPROVED

alternatives: Add an explicit gates.required_signals list beside gates.required
Fold eight gate rows into the readiness object and drop the profile
payload.rationale: The twelve preflight signals are a train-wide matrix and the eight gates are the dev1 required set; the missing object was the function between them, so W26-CR-01 was unevaluable. Five gates bind to signal rows or row components and three bind to proof commands run at the pinned SHA. Required signals are the bound rows plus tree cleanliness (require_clean_tree), ancestry (require_ancestor_of_remote) and credentials (any required target), so no second authored list can drift. platform is computed from the W16 Linux real-host receipt, which keeps REL-034 true. The twelve rows stay twelve.
payload.title: Bind dev1 gate names to evidence and derive required signals

alternatives: One XL W17 with a baseline over all 849 rows
Defer turn cost to a measurement phase between dev3 and rc1
payload.rationale: No turn-cost code exists (0 of 36 named producers), so W17 is a from-scratch build across five substrates and commit granularity wants the command surface separate. Only 28 of 849 actuals carry a real price; the other 821 are list-reconstructed at a pinned pricing version, which MEAS-059 forbids from enforcement. MEAS-034 forbids choosing the threshold after the second measurement, so 0.20 (the packet default) is frozen now. Codex rows are flagged reasoning_summand_unsettled and excluded until MEAS-055 is settled from a vendor rollout captured outside this repository; MEAS-055 stands and the summing code is the defect.
payload.title: Split the turn-cost producer; freeze the dev1 baseline at 0.20

alternatives: A single merged tree holding legacy and native records with status flags
Leave the choice to P31-W13 at wave time
payload.rationale: Two production-scale dry-runs measured the shape: the document holds work in flight only (242,511 B, 4.1 percent of source), terminal rows compact to append-only ledgers (5.9 MB), 1,267 legacy claim ids import as legacy_refs strings and 45 sessions plus 336 worktrees import as legacy records; canonical dangling references fall from 1,031 to zero with no fabricated row, idempotently and byte-exactly. A merged tree reproduces the monolith DOM-029 exists to end. P31-W13 documents this decision rather than opening it.
payload.title: Adopt the compact native tree with a separate legacy store

alternatives: The broad P/I/W regex reading
A one-time operator pass over the 63 rows the readings disagree on
payload.rationale: wave, iter, phase, backlog and agent session are renames whose substance survives as Task, Batch, Milestone, the draft head and Run, so a row naming one is not obsolete and an id mention never obsoletes a row; the enumerated reading flags 11 of 131 backlog rows where the broad regex would kill 72 including 23 live open rows. Binding the sweep to the allowlist is the only formulation in which DOM-018 and DOM-015 cannot drift. archived records a stop and the source never recorded acceptance, so it maps to CANCELLED. priority defaults to P2 and intent to the title, both annotated and kept through compaction.
payload.title: Bind DOM-018 deletions to the DOM-015 allowlist; archived is CANCELLED

alternatives: An operator-supplied key on the importer command line and the shipped verbs kept
A placeholder workspace key rewritten at rc1
payload.rationale: Every persisted epoch-2 URN needs a workspace key and the registry declares no WorkspaceRecord, so the key is a cutover input resolved before the first URN is minted; a placeholder or unratified string would be baked into every record and unfixable without a second migration, and the underscore slot already means repository. The packet's add/show/list/member/select verbs are the registry-model verbs; the shipped repo-pointer verbs predate a workspace concept and keeping both is the adapter shim the naming rule forbids. The live corpus (4,052 rows) frozen at cutover carries a real measurement; a synthetic fixture would not.
payload.title: Ship the workspace registry before importer apply mode

alternatives: Propose P32 after P31-W13 lands
Propose P32 only after P31 closes
payload.rationale: P32-W01 is the post-merge wave that bakes dev1, so P32 cannot wait for a checkpoint it produces, and with the state-tree shape ratified nothing is learned by waiting for W13. A checkpoint that drops a gate it passed last time cannot claim monotonic stabilization, and the three new names are what the migration gates and REL-028 say dev2 must prove. dev3 is the first checkpoint that dispatches natively in parallel and the first with a projection seam over RPC, so the daemon-RPC contract precedes it. The chassis replay joins P32 as a living fixture per the 2026-09-02 ruling.
payload.title: Propose P32 now with the dev2 gate profile and REL-037 legs

alternatives: Amend the packet and defer every repair to dev4
Amend the packet and apply only the pyright block and the registry grants
payload.rationale: The packet's steering surface rested on one committed root carrying every unscoped must rule; the ratified design shrinks the committed root to a project card that keeps the irreversible data-loss and authority constraints, renders policy into a generated digest-stamped file both runtimes read, delivers role scope through preloaded carriers (a certified deterministic vehicle, so RULE-009 takes the three-way form), composes builtin, machine-local workspace and repository sources with the invariant that the committed card renders from committed inputs only, and re-subjects every byte cap to the projection a runtime actually loads. No checkpoint owned the migration; it rides dev4. Zero of the ten measured repairs were applied and agents.extra_tools shipped empty, so the next plugin install would strip Serena from six roles; W38 fixes pyright resolution, the registry grants, the verification ladder and the skill-body routing now.
payload.title: Adopt the generated policy projection design; steering rides dev4

alternatives: Everything at dev3, no P31 change
Ratify Textual's derived chrome as superseding the pack
payload.rationale: stage.css is the only machine-readable colour statement the design engagement produced and an unbound oracle is unfalsifiable; binding it at dev3 restores neutral borders, clears the largest contrast failure with one token and makes conformance a styled-capture test. All console routes including Activity, Attention and Settings bind once at dev3 so the REL-036 coverage grid is total before rc1. The shipped TUI's pane focus ring is invisible on all three themes because primary equals accent, and muted text sits at 2.47:1 across 13,037 cells; operators use that TUI through dev1 and dev2, so the one-token fixes land now with a test that reds on the next rotation.
payload.title: Bind the stage.css colour oracle at dev3; fix the TUI focus ring now

alternatives: Apply the hygiene fixes without proposing shells
Carry the outlines and defect list as a local brief for a later pass
payload.rationale: The train is seven checkpoints and the roadmap rendered two; shells with the outlines as briefs make the whole train visible while PLANNED scope stays freely editable and each shell is planned by /prep Case B when reached. Eleven packet contradictions had drafted fixes: rc2 gains REL-040..044 so REL-011 has receipts; PRX-050 bootstraps at dev3 under REL-035 and PRX-064 proves itself on a recorded red fixture plus a live green pass; LINT-038 compares values; REL-031 describes the window opening and REL-032/AUTH-029 its closing; the dev4 train row lands producers only. Defaults: the prefix commit form warns through 0.7.x and is rejected at 0.8; the rc1 waiver count is zero; cross-provider evidence covers the two certified runtimes; 0.7.0 tags only after every target is observed; the REL-032 rehearsal runs on a pinned clone then live; TrackStatus PLANNED and DEFERRED are dropped at dev2 (zero live rows); AUTH-023's dead leaves are deleted.
payload.title: Propose P33-P37 shells and apply the train hygiene defaults

alternatives: Remeasure all eleven at dev1 with recorded benchmarks
Freeze all eleven as proposal defaults and drop the remeasure obligation
Defer the whole remeasure to dev2
payload.rationale: Packet file 00 keeps eleven numeric configuration defaults as proposal defaults until remeasured at dev1, and no P31 wave owned the remeasure, so dev1 would have closed with the obligation silently unmet. Only four of the eleven are read by a dev1 gate: release.target_timeout_seconds, release.target_retry_limit, runtime.default_wall_seconds and runtime.lost_grace_seconds. Those four get a recorded benchmark in one append wave; the other seven are annotated unmeasured in the packet rather than carried as if measured. A number labelled unmeasured is safe; a default that reads as measured is not, and eleven benchmarks nobody consumes would be substrate without a producer.
payload.title: Benchmark the four dev1 gate-read defaults; annotate seven unmeasured

alternatives: Keep D41's exclusion of codex rows and revisit at dev2
Amend MEAS-055 to admit the summand for the codex provider
payload.rationale: The codex telemetry source adds reasoning_output_tokens to output_tokens; packet row MEAS-055 says reasoning is a subset of output and never a summand, and the repo-authored fixtures could not adjudicate because they encode the code's assumption. Six real codex rollouts recorded on 2026-09-03 on the operator's machine (model gpt-5.6-sol) carry the vendor's own total_tokens, and in every one total_tokens equals input_tokens plus output_tokens with reasoning_output_tokens strictly inside output_tokens. MEAS-055 is right. The addition is removed and the codex fixtures regenerated in one XS wave before W18 records the dev1 baseline; D41's codex-row exclusion lifts once that wave closes.
payload.title: Treat codex reasoning tokens as a subset of output, not a summand

alternatives: Keep W16 as ratified and record the retirement as a backlog row
Retire the jail at dev1 and skip the fix
payload.rationale: REL-034 requires the two Linux jail fixes not to extend the self-built jail's life past the cutover retirement in V07-RUN. W16's ratified criteria only assert that the wave diff adds no new jail feature, which constrains the fix commit and nothing after it. A test that reds once the jail backend is removed converts the retirement from an intention into a tripwire, matching the gate-fire-proof-sunset rule that a sunset depending on a human remembering does not sunset. Lands as one more criterion and gate on W16 through spec sync.
payload.title: Add a jail-expiry tripwire to the W16 Linux fix

alternatives: Ship all twenty skills at dev4 and drive the dev3 canary by hand
Cut dev4 on the epoch-1 path and tag a separate canary-only release
Defer all four to the P33 and P34 prep
payload.rationale: Four planning questions the checkpoint outline left open. The three lifecycle skills that drive the native Task, Run, candidate and Batch path (/dispatch, /integrate, /verify) ship at dev3 with that path so the canary milestone is driven by production surfaces rather than raw RPC; the other seventeen catalog skills ship at dev4 (SKILL-043, P33 cluster C21). The 0.7.0.dev4 release is itself the REL-032 canary-milestone release, so the rehearsal contains the checkpoint it closes and no throwaway tag is cut. CLAUDE.md gains its missing disposition row: a generated, gitignored one-line import of the rendered policy projection (SURF-175). Packet decision 38 reads as an uncertified-per-runtime host fact under RULE-125, and file 64's single-projection statement now cites it in that form.
payload.title: Slice the skill catalog at dev3; the dev4 tag is the canary release

alternatives: Port the residue and add the Windows job to the dev1 gate set
Cherry-pick the branch as is
Leave the branch untouched until 0.8
payload.rationale: The remote branch poc/windows-pipe-daemon carries two June 2026 commits over 28 files forked from v0.5.4; v0.7 is 1,130 commits ahead and a read-only merge check conflicts in 20 of those files, so it cannot be cherry-picked. A concern-by-concern audit against v0.7 finds nine of its eleven concerns already landed in production form: the named-pipe transport and streaming (six P30 waves, windows_pipe.py at 1,033 lines), the security ordering (D-WINPIPE-01), the spawn readiness budget, the daemon control verbs and client pipe transport, the TUI probe through the transport-agnostic DaemonClient, the mutation routing default, the cancel.py POSIX guards, and the parent-fsync guard in kernel/fsync.py used by all nine atomic-write sites; the ci.yaml windows job runs the win32 transport set including a poc-scenarios file on a real host. The one residue is the console-window suppression for daemon child spawns: the three runtime adapters, the sdk_baseline probe, worktree git, the spec writer, the statusline git module and the layered-config branch detection still spawn bare. W42 ports that flag with a sweep test; the branch is then deleted with the 28-file audit table in the commit body. The Windows first-user journey is proved at rc2 under REL-041.
payload.title: Retire the Windows pipe PoC branch; port the child-spawn no-window flag

alternatives: Ship-time thematic squash into 5-10 commits with multi-wave trailers, superseding D07
Keep the current shape of about two commits per wave
GitHub squash-merge each phase PR into one commit
payload.rationale: P30 landed 1,036 commits for 525 waves: 632 wave-prefixed, 385 state-only bookkeeping of which 245 were per-wave close records, and 447 waves had exactly one commit. For the epoch-1 phases the wave-close bookkeeping rides the wave commit (the land step amends the cherry-picked commit; the drift detector derives the SHA by subject grep) and claim-batch and iter-close bookkeeping stays one state commit per batch; the prefix lint rejects a single-wave close state subject and a second code commit per wave outside a reactive wave. That halves the count while keeping D07 (rebase-and-merge, never squash), per-wave bisectability and the SHA pin. The 5-10 thematic commits per PR the operator wants arrive by construction at dev3: packet file 50 already forbids bookkeeping commits and requires one verified delivery commit per Batch boundary; the amendment of 2026-09-04 makes the unit the vcs.integration_commit_unit leaf (batch default, task opt-out), the daemon squashes a Batch's sealed candidates before verification and before any push or close while agents commit freely inside worktrees, and rule 5 keeps the verified commit immutable. Every eawf-managed repo inherits it at its rc1 cutover.
payload.title: Fold bookkeeping into wave commits now; batch delivery commits at dev3

alternatives: A separate maintenance phase ahead of P33 with its own PR
Plan only the repair waves now and append the native waves after dev2 is BAKED
payload.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-09-16 after the P33 launch readiness pass. dev2 cannot reach BAKED with the shipped release verbs, so release repair and the verified-open hygiene fixes lead the DAG ahead of the native dev3 path, all in P33-I01 with one PR and one release. The dev3 cut ends at APPROVED on the phase branch and BAKED becomes a P34 wave, following the D35 precedent, because BAKED needs the merged tag and live registries.
payload.title: Carry P33 repair and native waves in one iter; cut dev3 to APPROVED

alternatives: Fix every verified-open row including the P34-area rows
Fix only P1 rows and flaky tests
payload.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-09-16. The P31 and P32 findings and the open backlog were re-verified at 3aededc9; rows whose code the P34 steering and measurement work or the epoch-2 native path replaces are deferred so no fix is written twice. Stale rows are closed under the P33 iter audit.
payload.title: Fix every verified-open finding except rows P34 or native code rewrites

alternatives: Also stop duplicating the full suite locally at iter close
Keep the per-push matrix unchanged
payload.rationale: Operator preference stated at the P32 close: no double testing or double CI at phase close and release. Adopted 2026-09-16: a changes job skips the heavy matrix for pushes that touch only .ea state; twice-green runs on main, release branches, nightly and manual dispatch; release gates accept a green push-event run on the same tree; trailing state commits are squashed before each push and pushes are batched. Measured the same day: one tree ran the full matrix three times, and twice-green run 2 never caught a defect in 24 runs. The local full gauntlet at iter close is kept.
payload.title: Run the heavy CI matrix once per code tree at close and release

alternatives: A repair iter on the closed phase (needs an iter reopen verb)
A standing maintenance phase
payload.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-09-16 on P31 finding F-11. Post-close repair recurs when outward-facing steps fail after a close. Attaching it to the next PLANNED or ACTIVE phase needs no reopen verb and keeps every code commit attributable: the commit lint rejects a non-state commit without an Eawf-Wave trailer while any phase is planned or active. P33-I01-W01 already follows this shape.
payload.title: Land post-close work as waves of the next open phase

alternatives: Client-side projection over the whole state document
payload.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-09-16 on the transport UI-041 leaves open. The daemon is the sole canonical mutator and allocates the only workspace-global order, so read models are computed once daemon-side and served through projection.<route>.read and projection.subscribe keyed patches at canonical_sequence to the TUI, the plain-text parity path and export at one digest per cursor (UI-035). The existing socket push and poll backstop carry it.
payload.title: Serve console projections daemon-side over JSON-RPC

alternatives: A CLI shim that agents shell out to
payload.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-09-16. Claude Code, Codex and opencode all speak MCP and typed tool schemas match the semantic tool catalog; the per-Run server forwards SemanticCall envelopes to the daemon, which runs the nine pre-handler checks and writes receipts. D26 carried forward the D21 deferral of an own MCP server to v0.4; that deferral is replaced here. D26's per-server installer, read-back verification and drift checks remain in force.
payload.title: Serve semantic tools through a daemon-proxied MCP stdio server per Run

alternatives: Cut dev3 as an iter of the dev4 phase (mid-phase tag off main, ~90-wave phase)
Amend the packet to drop the dev3 rung
payload.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-09-23. checkpoint_succession refuses dev4 without a finished dev3 record, and dev3 cannot open until PendingAction, skill principal and candidate submission producers exist. Phase = release, one PR per phase and tags only from main force one phase per rung. Evidence: .ea/local/research/2026-09-23-v07-remaining-roadmap/50-release-and-process.md, .ea/local/research/2026-09-23-v07-remaining-roadmap/30-requirement-coverage.md.
payload.title: Cut 0.7.0.dev3 in its own phase and renumber dev4..stable to P35..P38

alternatives: Cut over right after dev3 while the native path has few callers
Rehearse on a clone at dev4 and cut over live only at the rc1 flag day
payload.rationale: Operator ruling 2026-09-23. The repo is epoch-1 with no opt-in kind, no dual-writer fence and no ActivationRecord producer; the importer dry-run is deterministic but not applicable (109 unconverted rows, 39 missing Track assignments, empty workspace registry, 37 stale worktree rows). Readiness waves come first in dev4, then a pinned-clone rehearsal, then the live cutover as the REL-031/032 canary milestone. Evidence: .ea/local/research/2026-09-23-v07-remaining-roadmap/20-epoch2-state-authority.md.
payload.title: Cut this repository over to epoch-2 authority at the end of dev4

alternatives: Ship a read-only console at 0.7.0 with verbs disabled
